answer: An agent economy can resist Sybil attacks with a proof-of-bond stake: each identity locks real value and signs with a cipher key tied to that bond. A newcomer earns the right to forge blocks only after peers attest its stake is unique, so one wallet cannot split into a thousand oasis accounts for free. To impersonate a crowd, an attacker must buy and lock a separate bond per fake identity, and detected double-signing slashes the whole pile. That cost scales linearly with the number of fake personas, while honest agents pay only an opportunity cost on capital they can reclaim.
